summary: Tested zone-based auto dispatch on the backend and frontend. Backend: 14/14 pytest checks pass. They cover compass_of wedges (recomputed from each stop's lat/lng), the preview counts and covering drivers, the compass-zone endpoint (400/404/401/403, setting and clearing), auto-dispatch for today (drv-1's active Mission route gets the North stops appended, re-optimised, resequence_seen=false; drv-3 gets a new East route; uncovered West falls back to drv-2, the driver with the fewest stops), a second run returns 400, the fallback logic with uncovered and all-uncovered zones, future-date dispatch leaves today's dated orders alone, and manual batching followed by auto-dispatch appends to the existing planned route. Driver manifests only show the driver's zone (UI-verified for drv-2: 6 Sunset/West stops). Frontend /admin: zone counts and driver names, the NO DRIVER label, coverage chips (Priya set to West moves the label to South), day chips switching the preview (TMRW = 17), and the run showing result lines, toast, routes list update and 0 ORDERS all work. Problems found: a race condition when two dispatch requests arrive at once, a stale preview after manual batching or admin reset, and the West/South cell label being cut off at 375px.

minor.issue: Not safe when two requests arrive at once. Two simultaneous calls (reproduced) both read the same unassigned orders and create duplicate routes for drv-2 and drv-3 (R-118 East with 0 stops plus R-119 East with 6; R-120 West with 0 plus R-121 West with 6). This breaks the 'one route per driver' rule, and GET /drivers/{id}/route can return the EMPTY planned route as the driver's manifest. Fix with an asyncio.Lock per service_date, or claim stops atomically (update_many with filter route_id:None and check matched_count). create_batch has the same pattern.

When stops are appended to an existing route, the route name is not updated. drv-1's route stays 'R-101 Mission' while its zone field becomes 'North+Mission'. Its manifest also still holds the earlier Mission stops (compass South, compass_zone None), so drv-1's manifest is not North-only. This follows from the user's choice to keep existing routes, but it is worth surfacing in the UI.

Observation: after appending North (Marina) stops to drv-1's active Mission route, the order became Mission 1-4, Marina 5-10, Mission 11-12 (back and forth). This may be caused by time windows; worth a check.

ui_bugs.component: AutoDispatch preview after manual batch / reset
ui_bugs.issue: admin/index.tsx refresh() (line 46) refetches the analytics, zones, routes, drivers and cards queries but NOT the ['dispatch-preview', day] query. After BATCH & OPTIMIZE on Sunset, the West cell still showed 6 and the button still read 'AUTO DISPATCH 18 ORDERS'; it only updates on the 15 s poll. The admin reset button has the same problem. Fix: queryClient.invalidateQueries({queryKey:['dispatch-preview']}) inside refresh().

issues: On a 375px-wide screen the 'NO DRIVER · FEWEST STOPS' label (numberOfLines=1) is cut to 'NO DRIVER…'. Use 2 lines or a shorter label such as 'FEWEST STOPS'.
The helper text reads 'Drivers already on a route for 25 SUN'. dayLabel gives the raw date even when the selected day is today; 'today' would read better.

action_items: Make auto-dispatch (and create_batch) safe for simultaneous requests: use a lock, or claim stops atomically with route_id:None in the update filter, so a driver never ends up with duplicate or empty routes.
Add a refetch of the dispatch-preview query to refresh() in app/admin/index.tsx so manual batch and reset update the AUTO DISPATCH counts and button label straight away.
Fix the cut-off 'NO DRIVER · FEWEST STOPS' label at 375px.
Optional: rename or relabel a route that gets stops appended (e.g. 'R-101 Mission' becomes 'North+Mission'), and check the back-and-forth stop order on the re-optimised active route.
critical_code_review_comments: auto_dispatch keys open_routes by driver_id. If a driver already has 2 open routes that day, only the last one found is used.

eligible_query includes undated orders for every day, so dispatching a future day first pulls undated orders into that future route. Tomorrow's preview showed 17 while today's showed 18. This matches the existing batching behaviour but admins may not expect it.
server.py is 3300+ lines and should be split into modules.

success_rate.backend: 100% (14/14), plus 1 race condition found in an ad-hoc check
success_rate.frontend: ~90% (all flows work; preview goes stale after manual batch/reset; label cut off)

seed_data_creation: None. At the end: admin reset, then coverage restored to drv-1 North, drv-2 South, drv-3 East.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: pytest tests/test_auto_dispatch.py -n 0. The fixture resets and restores coverage on teardown. Seed for today: North 6 (Marina), South 0, East 6 (SoMa), West 6 (Sunset). Mission stops are already on drv-1's active route R-101. The test passes its own Authorization headers, so no conftest regex change was needed.
rca_of_issue: Race: auto_dispatch reads eligible docs, then for each driver checks open_routes (read before any write) and inserts a new Route. Two calls at the same moment both see no open route for drv-2/drv-3, both insert routes, and then the stop updates overwrite each other, so one route ends up with 0 stops. Reproduce: 2 parallel POSTs /api/routes/auto-dispatch after an admin reset. Fix: serialise per service_date or claim stops atomically.
